h1: # Annual Message Volume: Dan vs. Suz
body:
> **RE-CHECKED [2026-09-04] — the premise gained material and the arithmetic is
> untouched.** [[wiki/people/suzanne-frank]] gained a section on six dated
> messages naming Judge Fred Adams, including her report of his death
> (2020-05-24). **No volume figure on this page is affected** — the messages
> were always in the corpus and always counted; what changed is that somebody
> read six of them. Nothing withdrawn.


> **RE-CHECKED [2026-08-28]:** flagged stale against
> [[wiki/people/suzanne-frank]] (2026-08-28), which added a new
> 2013–2014 eviction/concealment episode (Alexis Armel, the washing
> machine). No message-volume figure this page draws on is touched. **No
> claim on this page is affected.**

[[wiki/people/suzanne-frank|Suz]]'s page already states the finding in
prose — she outwrites Dan in every year but two, and the gap widens after
2018 until she is sending twice what he does. Read as a chart rather than a
table, the shape has a structure the prose doesn't foreground: a clean
two-phase pattern with one hinge, not a gradual drift.

## What the chart shows

**Phase one (2015–2016): Dan ahead, narrowly.** In the relationship's first
fourteen months — corpus start 2015-11-17 through the end of 2016 — Dan
sends more than Suz in both years: 281 to 267 in the opening seven weeks,
2,453 to 2,132 across all of 2016. Neither margin is large (5% and 13%
respectively), but the direction is consistent across a full calendar year,
which is long enough that it is not simply the volatility of a small
partial-year sample.

**The hinge (2017): a near-exact tie that resolves the other way.** 1,850
to 1,866 — the closest year in the whole series, and the last year Dan is
even competitive. From here the relationship's volume balance never returns
to his favor.

**Phase two (2017–2026): Suz ahead, and increasingly so.** Every year from
2017 onward, Suz sends more, and the ratio climbs rather than holding
steady: roughly 1.14:1 in 2018, widening past 1.5:1 by 2024–25 and reaching
**1.94:1 in 2026** (619 to 1,204) — Suz is sending essentially two messages
for every one of Dan's by the record's most recent year. 2018 is also the
single largest year on either side (4,191 for Suz, 3,066 for Dan), which is
the year [[wiki/people/fran-coldren|Fran]] died and the estate dispute
opened — volume peaks for both of them at once, inside a widening gap
rather than resetting it.

## What this does and does not establish

It establishes that the asymmetry is not a fixed disposition running the
whole length of the relationship — it is a two-phase pattern with a
specific pivot year (2017), and treating "she writes more" as true of the
whole eleven-year record obscures that the first two years ran the other
way.

It does **not** establish why 2017 is the hinge. Suz's own page does not
name a specific event dating to that year that would explain the reversal,
and this page does not speculate one. It also does not establish whether
the widening after 2018 tracks a specific cause (the estate dispute, her
financial deterioration, the general drift of the relationship) or is
simply what an already-reversed asymmetry does when nothing intervenes to
correct it — both are consistent with the same numbers.

## Falsifiers

1. A message-content read of 2017 that shows the near-tie is driven by a
   single short-lived event (an argument, a crisis) rather than a genuine
   trend inflection — this would relocate the hinge to a different year or
   dissolve it into noise.
2. A per-month breakdown of 2018–2020 showing the widening gap is flat or
   reversing rather than monotonic — the yearly aggregates here could hide
   a non-monotonic path that a coarser read would miss.

## Gaps

- No mechanism is proposed for the 2017 hinge; the message content around
  it has not been read specifically for this question.
- 2021 and 2023 are partial years in the source table (to April; from
  August), which is why they sit lower than the surrounding years — this
  chart plots the partial-year totals as given rather than annualizing them,
  and a reader comparing bar heights across those two years against full
  years should account for that before drawing a conclusion from magnitude
  alone.
